17 A sample of gas is sealed in a cylinder by a piston. The frictionless piston is free to move, so that
the pressure of the gas remains constant at 1.80  105
Pa.
The gas initially occupies a volume of 2.40  10–4
m3.
The gas now does 14.4 J of work.
What is the volume of the gas after doing this work?
A
0.80  10–4
m3
B
1.60  10–4
m3
C
3.20  10–4
m3
D
4.00  10–4
m3

hints: Notice the pressure stays constant at $1.80 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ while the gas does $14.4 \text{ J}$ of work starting from $2.40 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$.
For constant pressure, work done by a gas is linked to volume change by $W = p\Delta V$, so first find $\Delta V = W/p$.
Calculate $\Delta V$ in $\text{m}^3$ and add it to the initial volume because a gas that does work on the piston expands.
walkthrough: Identify the constant-pressure expansion: $p = 1.80 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$, $V_1 = 2.40 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$, and work done by gas $W = 14.4 \text{ J}$.
State the governing rule for work at constant pressure: $W = p\Delta V = p(V_2 - V_1)$.
Rearrange for the volume increase: $\Delta V = W/p$.
Substitute with units: $\Delta V = 14.4 / (1.80 \times 10^5) = 8.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^3 = 0.80 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$.
Add the increase to the starting volume because doing work means expansion: $V_2 = 2.40 \times 10^{-4} + 0.80 \times 10^{-4} = 3.20 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$.
Check units: $\text{Pa} \times \text{m}^3 = \text{J}$, so the calculation is homogeneous. This is option C.

A.explanation: This subtracts the volume change from the initial volume, but gas doing work expands so volume must increase.

B.explanation: This is the initial volume minus $0.80 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$, which treats expansion as compression.

C.explanation: The change $\Delta V = W/p = 0.80 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$ added to $2.40 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$ gives $3.20 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$.

D.explanation: This adds too large a change, from dividing $14.4 \text{ J}$ by a smaller pressure or mis-handling powers of ten.
